builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HyPAIC: Personal AI Computer with High Bandwidth Flash for High Performance Trillion-Parameter LLM Inference
summary: HyPAIC replaces LPDDR-only unified memory in personal AI computers with a split design storing read-only model weights in high-bandwidth flash (HBF) and mutable runtime data (KV cache) in LPDDR. The cost is a hardware platform that does not yet exist commercially: HBF specifications are still evolving, and the design must manage HBF's access latency, limited write endurance, page-level access granularity, and unresolved power and cooling demands. The approach can fail because all results are simulation-based, prefetching may not hide latency for irregular access patterns, and write endurance constrains the read-only placement assumption.
rationale: This is a hardware architecture proposal requiring HBF devices that are not commercially available, so a practitioner with one 24 GB GPU can only track it as a signal that future on-premises trillion-parameter inference hardware is being designed, not adopt or test anything today.
technique: HBF-based weight storage for personal AI computers

claims.statement: HyPAIC replaces LPDDR-only unified memory in personal AI computers with a split design storing read-only model weights in high-bandwidth flash (HBF) and mutable runtime data (KV cache) in LPDDR. The cost is a hardware platform that does not yet exist commercially: HBF specifications are still evolving, and the design must manage HBF's access latency, limited write endurance, page-level access granularity, and unresolved power and cooling demands. The approach can fail because all results are simulation-based, prefetching may not hide latency for irregular access patterns, and write endurance constrains the read-only placement assumption.

One HyPAIC system achieves up to 1.04x end-to-end throughput and up to 3.59x TDP-normalized throughput versus the aggregate of eight baseline systems during 1T-parameter MoE inference, and up to 4x concurrent tasks sustaining 50 decode TPS for small models (simulation-based).
